title: Etale acyclicity of affine schemes with closed separably closed points
statement: Let $T$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Assume every point of $|T|$ is closed (its singleton is closed) and every residue field $\kappa(t)=\mathcal O_{T,t}/\mathfrak m_t$ [def-weil-residue-field] is separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed]. For every abelian sheaf $F$ on the small etale site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and every integer $i>0$, $$H^i(T_{\mathrm{et}},F)=0,$$ with cohomology defined as right derived global sections [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Neither noetherianity nor finite type nor finiteness or torsion of $F$ is assumed.

proof.text: Write T as Spec A. The Mathlib equivalence PrimeSpectrum.isClosed_singleton_iff_isMaximal turns closedness of every singleton into maximality of every prime. Apply lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-spectrum-profinite and transfer the three topological instances along T.isoSpec.hom.homeomorph.

Closed singletons make the specialization order discrete. Every point is therefore maximal in that order. Mathlib ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_coheight and Order.IsMax.coheight_eq_zero show that every stalk has Krull dimension zero. Its residue field is separably closed by hypothesis, so lem-weil-pbc-dimension-zero-local-strictly-henselian makes each stalk strictly henselian.

For an etale map Y -> T and y over x, choose an affine open V around y. Pull Spec(O_T,x) back along V -> T and choose a point over y and the closed point. Apply lem-sbc-strict-henselian-etale-neighbourhood-section to obtain a section over Spec(O_T,x). Its composition into V corresponds to a ring map Gamma(V) -> O_T,x over Gamma(T). The map Gamma(T) -> Gamma(V) is finitely presented. Apply Mathlib RingHom.EssFiniteType.exists_eq_comp_ι_app_of_isColimit to the stalk colimit, with the natural transformation given by restriction from Gamma(T), to factor the map over Gamma(U) for some open neighborhood U of x, maintaining the structure-map equation. Taking Spec and composing U -> Spec Gamma(U) gives a section U -> Y. These constructions and their compatibility identities are fully proved in the private exists_section_near_of_strictlyHenselian helper.

Construct the explicit open-subscheme inclusion i:T.Opens -> T.Etale. The fully faithful forgetful functor identifies it with the inclusion supplied by lem-weil-pbc-zariski-etale-core; transfer continuity along this isomorphism. Thus restricting any etale abelian sheaf along i gives a Zariski sheaf. For an epimorphism F -> G, Mathlib Sheaf.isLocallySurjective_iff_epi' supplies etale local lifts of each section of G(T). The covering-family description of the small etale topology gives a covering member above each x. The section on an open neighborhood furnished in step 3 pulls that lift back to a Zariski local lift; naturality verifies its image is the restriction of the original section.

Refine this open cover of the profinite space by a finite disjoint clopen cover using Mathlib IsOpenCover.exists_finite_nonempty_disjoint_clopen_cover. Pull back the local lifts to these clopens. Distinct pairwise intersections are empty, on which the sheaf of groups has only its zero section. The lifts are therefore compatible and the sheaf gluing theorem gives a global lift; separatedness verifies its image. This includes the empty scheme, for which the finite cover has no members. Hence evaluation at i(top), a terminal etale object, preserves epimorphisms. The full proof is the private surjective_top_of_profinite_local_lifts helper.

The constant-sheaf/evaluation adjunction constantSheafAdj and Adjunction.map_projective send the projective group ULift Z to a projective constant sheaf, because the right adjoint preserves epimorphisms by steps 4-5. Sheaf.H is Ext from this constant sheaf. Write i=n+1 and apply Mathlib Abelian.Ext.subsingleton_of_projective to obtain the required vanishing.
